---
title: Connectors
description: How a connector fits a Marfa plugin, where its key comes from, and what the instance keeps so a run can stop and resume.
job: A builder sees how a connector fits a Marfa plugin.
kind: concept
---

A **connector** is a program outside the server. It registers with the instance, reads another service (its vendor), and writes what it finds as items. It can also carry changes made in Marfa back to the vendor. A program that reads and writes with a key, and never registers, is not a connector.

The server never runs a connector, and it never calls a vendor. The usual connector is part of a **Marfa plugin**: a bundle an owner installs, from [withmarfa/plugins](https://github.com/withmarfa/plugins), that brings a connector, its types, or both. That is not the [Marfa plugin for agents](/connect-your-agent).

## A Marfa plugin

Installing the plugin records its types, each with a description and [guidance](/catalog/type-definition#descriptions-and-guidance), and its connector. The connector names its source, the kinds of record it brings, its settings, and that it runs on a host. [Build a Marfa plugin](/build/connector) makes one and installs it from its source folder.

For that connector, **a host is the way it runs**. The host mints the key and starts the process. [Build a connector host](/build/connector-host) is what the host does before that start. Marfa doesn't publish a host yet.

The owner keeps every other setting in Marfa, and a mapping chooses where each kind of record lands. The process reads both at the start of a run. Its environment holds `MARFA_API_URL`, `MARFA_API_KEY` and [telemetry](/reference/connector-kit#telemetry), and nothing else.

## The key

The [connector kit](/reference/connector-kit) takes the key its host mints. It reads that key back on every start and **refuses a key of any other shape**, then the process exits with code 3. The key holds the connector's source as its own, and write on the types and connection types the connector writes, and nothing else.

A key holds one registration. An app's sign-in cannot register a connector. A key no host minted can start a connector that declares no settings. Marfa opens settings only to a host-minted key, so a connector that declares settings stops on any other key.

## What the instance keeps

The instance keeps what a connector needs to resume, so it can stop and move without losing its place. The state document, the agreements and the problems belong to the key's **source**, not to one key.

| What | What it's for |
| --- | --- |
| A registration | Names the connector and the types it holds read only, and shows its last heartbeat and how recent runs went. |
| A state document | Where the connector stopped at the vendor. |
| Agreements | What the connector and the vendor last agreed about one item. |
| A hold | Lets one process write at a time. |
| Inbound deliveries | What a vendor posted, for the connector to check and then read the vendor. |

A type the connector does not carry back is named on the registration. Its items read `read_only: true`. Marfa refuses no write for that flag: the connector puts the edit back on its next run. [Write a connector on the API](/build/connector-without-the-kit#declare-the-types-you-dont-carry-back) is where that list is sent.

## A connector on its own

A connector that is not part of a Marfa plugin still [registers itself](/reference/api/connectors/registerConnector) with a working key, and it runs where you start it. [Write a connector on the API](/build/connector-without-the-kit) is that run, in order. The kit refuses the key when that connector declares settings.

The rules are in the [connectors](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/connectors.md) and [plugins](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/plugins.md#connector-hosts) chapters of the contract.
